Full statement for WikiLeaks release "OutlawCountry", CIA's covert kernel module for Linux (link to release in comments)

Has anyone found a way to identify infected computers?

I'm not a sysadmin or anything like that, can someone explain the consequences of what could happen if an infected computer made it onto your secured network in a commercial setting?

It seems to have a lot more functionality than simple spyware.

A simple way to put this.

It modifies your firewall to duplicate all traffic inbound/outbound from the system so it not only goes to its intended destination but also another destination (some gov server).

The wording also seems to imply that the module also listens to inbound traffic, most likely for instructions to do other bad stuff.

It claims that this only works on a default kernel (supplied by CentOS or RedHat) but most organizations do not re-compile their kernels from scratch. It will be interesting to learn more about this because if it only works on a default kernel provided by the maintainer it is likely taking advantage of a very specific condition and could be an intentional configuration.

The impact to this is that it creates a system on your network that could be used as a pivot to attack other systems or to steal data.

To combat this, a properly designed IDS (intrusion detection system) and network monitoring would be ideal. Now, this will only help you detect that you were compromised if you know what to look for. It wont stop the initial attack and you will probably leak some data. DLP (data loss prevention) systems usually integrate with other network monitoring systems to attempt to block specific types of data from leaving a network.

I previously setup a DLP system that would scan all outgoing email for specific strings that looks like Social Security Numbers or Credit Card Numbers and would block the email from leaving the network without direct intervention from the security office.

Hope that helps.
